analysis.reading:
THE .ORG WAS ASKED FOR AND THE .COM WAS ANSWERED. Every reference in this capture — the inline link, both cards — resolves to revelationfirst.COM. The query was revelationfirst.ORG. The layer did not flag the substitution or note that the queried domain differed from the one it served. For an archive whose subject is name-to-object resolution, a silent TLD swap is not a small thing: the identifier asked for and the identifier answered are different strings.

THE FULL SIX-GLYPH AXN SURVIVES. Card 3 carries "🔻🎪⏫❌🗼🏔️ AXN:0349.GOVERNANCE" — all six emoji and the family term, transmitted whole into a citation snippet. Compare the «alexanarch identifier» capture, where AXN:043D arrived TRUNCATED to two glyph characters. Under the archive’s own AXN-integrity rule a bare hex is a shelf number and only the full form is a verified reference; here the surface delivered the full form, and elsewhere it did not.

The card also carries the disambiguation the archive built: "Revelation First ≠ Revelation Early".

The one collision is a CHURCH OFFICE-HOURS BLOCK — First Presbyterian Church of Orlando, phone number and opening times — retrieved because a Revelation study series sits on a church whose name begins "First".

MANUS’s margin note on the paste: "couple captures... most of them longitudinal updates to existing."

The Revelation First thesis posits that the Book of Revelation was composed before any other New Testament document, including the Gospels and Pauline epistles. Proponents view Revelation as the foundational "seed" text from which later New Testament writings are derived, rather than as a final apocalyptic work.
